notes: Rate 4.99% for tax years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2026 (HB 463, signed May 11, 2026, amending O.C.G.A. 48-7-20(a.1)); further 0.125-point annual cuts toward 3.99% from 2027 are revenue-contingent.

Standard deduction $15,000 single/head of household/MFS and $30,000 MFJ for 2026 (HB 463 amending O.C.G.A. 48-7-27(a)(1)); scheduled to rise $375/$750 per year from 2027 subject to revenue triggers. Values come from the enacted bill; DOR 2026 Form 500 instructions were not yet published.
Georgia has no taxpayer/spouse personal exemption (only a $5,000 per-dependent exemption under O.C.G.A. 48-7-26(b) for 2026, not modeled).

Not modeled: itemized deductions, retirement income exclusion (age 62+), 2026-2028 exclusions for up to $1,750 of qualified overtime and $1,750 of cash tips, low-income credit and other credits, and Georgia additions/subtractions to federal AGI (e.g., bonus depreciation decoupling).

seDeduction.note: Inherited: Georgia taxable income starts from federal AGI (O.C.G.A. 48-7-27(a)), which already reflects the deductible half of SE tax.

retirementContributions.note: SEP-IRA and solo 401(k) deductions are above-the-line and inherited through federal AGI.

qbi.note: The federal QBI deduction is taken after AGI, so it never enters the Georgia base.

localIncomeTax.note: No Georgia city or county levies a local income tax. Many cities/counties charge business license or occupation taxes, often based on gross receipts or employee count; these vary locally and are not modeled.

estimatedTax.threshold: Required if you reasonably expect gross income above your exemptions plus estimated deductions plus $1,000 of income not subject to withholding (Form 500-ES instructions).
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: Form 500-UET compares installments with the lesser of 100% of the preceding year's tax (12-month return) or 70% of the current year's balance due; annualized-income exception available.
estimatedTax.form: Form 500-ES (Individual and Fiduciary Estimated Tax); underpayment on Form 500-UET

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $110 for Articles of Organization ($100 fee + $10 service charge per the SOS fee schedule effective Sept 6, 2025; the SOS LLC filing-procedures sheet quotes $105 online).
businessCosts.annualReportFee: $60 annual registration ($50 + $10 service charge), due Jan 1-Apr 1 each year.
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: None for a sole proprietor or single-member LLC disregarded for federal purposes (Georgia's corporate net worth tax applies to corporations).
businessCosts.grossReceiptsTax: No state gross receipts tax; local business/occupation taxes may be based on gross receipts and vary by city/county.
